learning_outcomes.text: Approach the reality of underdevelopment and marginalization.

Acquire a global and supportive vision of reality, complementing conventional technical education to achieve comprehensive training that includes the ethical principles that should govern professional practice.
Acquire specific professional training in the field of technological cooperation and development.
Participate in a debate forum on technical cooperation and development at the University of Oviedo.
Students with a greater critical sense, respect for diversity, and capacity for participation in social activities.
Approach the reality of underdevelopment and marginalization.

Acquire a global and supportive vision of reality, complementing conventional technical education to provide students with comprehensive training that includes the ethical principles that should govern their professional practice.
Acquire specific professional training in the field of technological cooperation and development.
Participate in a debate forum on technical cooperation and development at the University of Oviedo.
Put into practice critical thinking, respect for diversity, and the ability to participate in social activities.

syllabus_topics: Cooperation for development: methods and agents.
Infrastructure, construction, and materials technologies in development cooperation.
Cooperation projects for development based on energy supply to rural communities and other disadvantaged groups.
Digital policy: digital divides; biases in design and use; new rights and properties; ICTs as agents of change and social control.
Atmospheric pollution: impacts of climate change.
teaching_methods: Group work simulating NGO volunteer teams

assessment_methods.method: Final exam (project report and verbal presentation)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary assessment, a minimum of 75% attendance (44 hours) is required, otherwise the grade will be 'Not Presented'. The final grade is calculated as: FINAL_GRADE = EX_FIN x 0.3 + (P1 + P2 + P3 + P4 + P5 + P6) x 0.1 + A x 0.05 + PA x 0.05. A minimum of 5 points from this formula is needed to pass. For extraordinary assessments, the final grade is calculated as: FINAL_GRADE = EX_EXTRA x 0.4 + (P1 + P2 + P3 + P4 + P5 + P6) x 0.1, with a minimum of 5 points to pass. For extraordinary assessments, students must inform the faculty at least 4 weeks in advance and submit reports at least 48 hours before the exam.
